citation: Yip PSF, Fu KW, Yang KCT, Ip BYT, Chan CLW, Chen EYH, Lee DTS, Law FYW, Hawton K. The effects of a celebrity suicide on suicide rates in Hong Kong. Journal of Affective Disorders. 2006;93(1–3):245–252. doi:10.1016/j.jad.2006.03.015.
title: The effects of a celebrity suicide on suicide rates in Hong Kong
abstract: Population-level observational study examining suicide rates in Hong Kong after the highly publicized suicide of a celebrity in 2003, with comparisons to preceding and historical periods and qualitative review of case files.
intervention_or_exposure: high-profile celebrity suicide with extensive media coverage
uncertainty: Excess-suicide statistical analyses were based on aggregated population data.
Observational design cannot isolate media exposure from all concurrent influences.
methods: population suicide-rate comparison across time periods
qualitative review of case files and suicide notes

evidence_claims.statement: Suicides increased after the extensively reported celebrity suicide compared with reference periods, with a particularly marked pattern among men aged 25–39 and many deaths by jumping.
evidence_claims.intervention_or_exposure: high-profile celebrity suicide with extensive media coverage

provenance.source_span: The abstract reports a significant post-event increase, especially among men aged 25–39, many of whom died by jumping.

evidence_claims.statement: Case-file review found frequent references to the celebrity, supporting a plausible media-related influence while remaining observational evidence.
evidence_claims.intervention_or_exposure: high-profile celebrity suicide with extensive media coverage

provenance.source_span: The report notes that the celebrity’s name was often mentioned in case files or notes.

evidence_claims.statement: The authors explicitly note that the statistical evidence for excess suicides was based on aggregated data, limiting individual-level inference.
evidence_claims.intervention_or_exposure: high-profile celebrity suicide with extensive media coverage

provenance.source_span: The article notes that excess-suicide statistical results were based on aggregated data.

limitations: Concurrent societal or media factors may confound before/after comparisons.
applicability: Relevant to responsible media-reporting policy and population-level postvention planning.
Does not identify which individual media consumers will be affected.
safety_boundaries: Do not use exposure to media coverage as an individual suicide-risk score.
Do not infer individual causality from aggregate population changes.
